The Power of the People

The whole history of ordinary people against the people who ruled them, from the first farming towns to today.

Did ordinary people ever take power from the people who ruled them? For most of history, no. Rulers held it, everyone else lived under it, and every challenge died with the people who made it. Then, after 1800, it happened once, in one domain, and it has not been repeated.

The domain was formal political status: the vote, legal equality, national sovereignty, now held by billions of people whose ancestors held none of them. The rest of the record, the long stretch where rulers seem to be losing, sorts three ways. Sometimes the loss was real. Sometimes it was a loan, recalled within weeks. And very often it was a change of costume, from a lord you could petition or flee to a system you cannot argue with.

The Power of the People · Evening Report

Four numbers, one argument

The transfer was real in one domain. These are the numbers that bound it.

76% / 2%Global wealth, top tenth against bottom half
The richest 10 percent of humanity owns 76 percent of global wealth. The bottom half owns 2 percent. World Inequality Report 2022.
35% → 9.9%United States union membership
About 35 percent of workers were union members at the peak in 1954. In 2024, 9.9 percent were. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
91 / 88Autocracies against democracies, 2024
The V-Dem count for 2024 found 91 autocracies and 88 democracies, the first time autocracies have outnumbered democracies in over twenty years.
1% / 55%Income misreported to the IRS
Income subject to withholding is misreported at about 1 percent. Income subject to little or no reporting is misreported at about 55 percent.

THE BOARD

Why The Board exists.

I don’t have a ton of time. It’s hard to keep up.

There are so many conflicting narratives, fed by conflicting interests. It feels hard to know what is true, and I know I’m not alone in that.

I often have questions I want answered, or things I don’t understand, that the news simply doesn’t cover. Not all of the time, but sometimes. When that happens, there is nowhere obvious to go for a straight answer.

In my ideal world, I build something useful to me. Something I enjoy reading. Because if I do, so will other people, and it will help them too.

The Board is a personal project. Everything here reflects my own views and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representative of my employer.
